insights.title: Rainfall has decreased
insights.body: Yearly rain went from about 972 mm to 765 mm.

insights.title: More very hot days
insights.body: Days at 35 °C or hotter went from about 71 to 84 a year. Heat at flowering cuts yields of rice, maize and most pulses.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Groundnut, Pigeon pea and Green gram score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: About 30 more scorching days a year by 2035
consequences.detail: Days at 35 °C or hotter are heading from about 77 to 107 a year. Heat during flowering kills pollen, so grain and pod set drop — Groundnut, Pigeon pea, Green gram and Cowpea are most exposed.
consequences.action: Sow so flowering misses the hottest weeks, or pick heat-tolerant varieties.

consequences.headline: Rain could fall 33% by 2035
consequences.detail: Yearly rain trends from about 854 mm to 575 mm.
consequences.action: Favour drought-tolerant crops and keep crop residue on the soil to hold moisture.

consequences.headline: In a dry year, rain can drop to about 309 mm
consequences.detail: That is 64% below the 854 mm average; about 1 year in 10 is this dry or worse. Groundnut and Soybean would fall short of water.
consequences.action: Keep a drought-tolerant crop in the plan as insurance.

consequences.headline: Crops will need about 366 mm more water than rain gives
consequences.detail: Rain minus crop water demand moves from -716 mm to about -1,082 mm a year.
consequences.action: Plan irrigation or water harvesting, or shift to crops that need less water.

consequences.headline: +1.2 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 26.7 °C to about 27.9 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.
